Forward planning  
Variation No.1 (Portarlington) and No.2 (Graiguecullen) to the County Development 
Plan 2021 - 2027  
Variation No.1 (Portarlington) and No.2 (Graiguecullen) were on public display from 25th 
February 2026 to 27th March 2026 (inclusive of both dates) where submissions were 
invited from members of the public and statutory bodies.  
 
Submissions 
 
A total of 15 no. submissions were received in relation to Variation No.1 (Portarlington) 
and 12 no. submissions were received in response to Variation No.2 (Graiguecullen).   
 
The submissions have all been summarised in a Chief Executive (CE) Report which has 
been circulated to the members of Laois County Council for each variation. This includes 
the CE opinion and recommendations to each of the submissions.   
 
Next Steps  
 
The Council will consider this report and decide on the recommendations at the May 
Council meeting.

The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant has been expanded, with effect from 31st March, 2026, 
to support bringing more vacant and derelict properties into use as homes. This includes the 
provision of top-up amounts to existing grant levels where vacant former commercial/public use 
buildings are being converted in their entirety into two or more residential units. 
 
From 31st March 2026, the following grants are also available: 
 
Vacant Above the Shop Grant 
 
A grant of up to €135,000 is available for the conversion or refurbishment of vacant above shop 
space into residential units for occupation as a principal private residence and/or for residential 
units), subject to appropriate planning permission being in place.  Where one residential unit is 
being created in the vacant above the shop space a grant of up to €95,000 will be available, where 
two residential units are being created up to €115,000 is available and where three or more units 
are created up to €135,000 is available. 
 
The Grant applies to vacant ‘above the shop’ space in buildings in cities, towns and villages, where 
the building was built prior to 2008 and the space/existing residential unit(s) have been vacant for 
two years or more prior to application. The ground floor commercial space may be vacant or in use 
at time of application but must be remaining in commercial use.  
 
Expert Advice Grant 
 
An Expert Advice Grant is available for Vacant Above the Shop Conversions and Conversion of 
former commercial / public use buildings to residential units.  The Expert Advice Grant provides 
funding of up to €5,000 towards having an appropriately qualified professional provide expert 
advice to the owner of;  
  
• 
A building with a commercial element and vacant above the shop space who may avail of 
the Vacant Above the Shop Grant to convert / refurbish the vacant space into residential 
unit/s, with the commercial element remaining. 
• 
A former vacant commercial / public use building who may avail of the Vacant Property 
Refurbishment Grant Conversion of former Commercial Building / public use building to 
convert the entire building into more than one residential unit. 
 
Only one Expert Advice grant can be applied for per building.  Applications can only be made by 
named individuals who own the building for which the advice grant is being applied, or who are 
actively engaged in purchasing the building. Where there is more than one owner of the building, 
all owners must be included on the application form. The Expert Advice Grant is not currently 
available to registered companies, developers, undertakings etc.

BUSINESS SUPPORT UNIT 
Local Enterprise Office 
National Enterprise Awards 2026 
Le Skinny Chef Ltd based in Portlaoise has been named a finalist in this year’s National Enterprise 
Awards and will represent Local Enterprise Office Laois in the Round Room at the Mansion House, 
Dublin on June 18th. The National Enterprise Awards celebrate the achievements of Ireland’s 
micro-enterprise sector and recognise the achievements of companies supported by the Local 
Enterprise Offices.  
 
Aymar Gourdet is a multi-award-winning chef and restaurateur. Le Skinny Chef Ltd. was founded 
in 2016 in Portlaoise, and the company specialises in artisanal French-Irish fusion sauces, soups, 
pesto’s and many more products. From an early age, Aymar was interested in cooking and opened 
his first gastronomic restaurant almost 30 years ago. After founding Le Skinny Chef Ltd, the 
demand for his products such as his Spreadable Wild Garlic Pesto and soups has been huge.  
Le Skinny Chef Ltd. is an excellent example of a local business who availed of a wide range of LEO 
supports such as LEAN, Green and Digital supports which helps to improve efficiencies, processes 
and digitalisation. Local Enterprise Office Laois has supported the business’s incremental growth 
in the form of both financial grant assistance and soft supports.  
 
The company has been approved business expansion grants which have helped to grow the 
business and was approved an Energy Efficiency grant. The company has also availed of a Trading 
Online Voucher to further develop their online presence and have availed of TAME grant to 
explore export markets. Aymar also took part in Phase 1 and Phase 2 of the Get Exporting 
Programme run by LEO Laois.  
 
Le Skinny Chef Ltd will go forward to represent Laois at the National Finals where there will be an 
announcement of winners from each region as well as the Overall winner. Categories this year 
include ‘Best Export Business,’ ‘Best Start-Up’ and ‘Innovation,’ along with “One to Watch” and a 
“Sustainability” award in addition to nine regional awards.

Portlaoise – Attanagh Greenway 
A Tender for the appointment of a Design Team, to undertake a Feasibility Study for the 
Portlaoise to Attanagh Greenway, has been completed.  TII approval for the approval is 
anticipated and the Design Team will commence the Study immediately thereafter.  
Urban Area Speed Limit Review 
The review of Urban Speed Limits is to be undertaken in accordance with the provisions 
of Department of Transport Circular RW21 of 2025.   Pre-consultations with statutory 
stakeholders has commenced. For National Roads, TII have been notified of four 
locations where LCC is proposing 30km/h speed limits, in accordance with the 
requirements of the Circular. Implementation of these speed limits requires the approval 
of TII.   
At present there are four locations at which the provisions of the Department of 
Transport Circular require speed limit reductions, namely: 
• 
Durrow N77 
• 
Mountmellick N80 
• 
Abbeyleix N77 
• 
Portlaoise N80 
Once all proposed new Urban Speed Limits are identified, it is proposed to commence 
public consultation for 30 days, likely to occur in June/July 2026. This is with a view to to 
adopting Bye-laws by 30th of October 2026, in accordance with the timeline outlined in 
Circular RW21 and for all new Urban Speed Limits to be in place by 31st March 2027.

areas.  Laois County Council received Department funding of €469,000 for 2026 and

encourages a joint approach between the local authority and groups of residents and 
landowners for the restoration of public roads.  Laois County Council received Department

98th Anniversary of First East West Transatlantic Flight 
 
Sunday 12th April saw the 98th anniversary of the first East West Transatlantic flight in 
which local Portlaoise man Colonel James Fitzmaurice was part of the three-man crew. 
This pioneering event in world aviation history is celebrated every year by the Colonel 
Fitzmaurice Commemoration Society in partnership with Laois Heritage Office.  
 
The annual commemorative event in Fitzmaurice place included speeches and a wreath 
laying ceremony attended by Cllr. Barry Walsh, Cathaoirleach of Laois County Council. 
This year, the commemoration event was followed by a discussion and Q&A session in 
Kavanagh’s Bar.  Laois Heritage Officer Thomas Carolan chatted to Brigadier General 
Rory O'Connor and Maj Gen Ralph James (R’td) of the Irish Air Corps and Teddy 
Fennelly, Colonel Fitzmaurice Commemorative Society, about the famous flight and the 
life of Col. James Fitzmaurice.  A short documentary of the flight and life of Col. 
Fitzmaurice (previously commissioned by Laois Heritage Office) was shown to attendees 
before the discussion began, which can viewed here: 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S7Lt9yFcIeg  
 
Laois Heritage Office is working closely with the Colonel Fitzmaurice Commemorative 
Society to plan the centenary celebrations in April 2028 which will feature a diverse 
programme of events including a state commemorative event.
